small_guidance:
- Fuse the softmax into a single persistent kernel: since N=8192 fits in registers with BLOCK_N=8192 and num_warps=16/32, you can avoid the separate softmax launch's extra read/write. Better, fuse GELU+row-max tracking into the GEMM epilogue by writing a split-K-free GEMM where each row's tiles compute online softmax stats — but at minimum, try num_warps=16 for the softmax kernel at BLOCK_N=8192.
- Add larger GEMM tiles to the autotune list (e.g. BLOCK_M=256, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=32/64, num_warps=8, num_stages=3) since M=N=K=8192 is a large square problem that favors big tiles; also try BLOCK_K=128 with num_stages=4.
- Drop the per-iteration k_remaining masks in the GEMM main loop (K=8192 is divisible by 32/64/128) — split into a masked tail-loop only when K%BLOCK_K!=0, so the hot loop becomes unmasked tl.load and the compiler can pipeline better.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a fused GEMM+GELU+softmax persistent kernel: one program per output row tile that streams over N-tiles, holding the full row in registers/SMEM. Use online softmax (running max m and normalizer l updated per N-tile) to fuse the row-reduction with the matmul epilogue, eliminating the intermediate (M,N) GELU tensor entirely (saves a 1024×8192 fp32 write+read = ~64MB of traffic).
- Alternatively, keep GEMM separate but make softmax a two-pass row-resident kernel with vectorized loads (float4) and BLOCK_N tiled (e.g. 1024) iterated within the program, so the (M,N) tensor is read exactly twice rather than via a wide single-block kernel that may spill at BLOCK_N=8192.
- Consider transposing W once at init (store as (in, out) contiguous) so the GEMM B operand has stride_bk=N, stride_bn=1 — contiguous on the inner axis — instead of relying on swapped strides of the original (out,in) layout, which currently makes the B loads strided.
